requirements.quote: `default_explorer` returns None (with a recorded note on the node) when the image model is not installed or not healthy on the model host; an explorer failure at render time degrades to no concept image with a warning, never fails the node
a cheap "is model installed" query (setup state or a models-serve probe)
style frames render with the image model absent
With the image model not installed, `studio run` builds style frames and boards through the scene builder, with a note on the node that concept images were skipped
With the model installed, concept images are still produced
No regression: `uv run pytest -q`, ruff, mypy
requirements.why: Host rules forbid running the full suite in lane; the targeted tests that reference every changed file run here, ruff and mypy run on the changed files, and CI runs the full suite.

deliverables.change: ModelRuntime.__init__ gains keyword `installed: Collection[str] | None = None`, stored as `self.installed: frozenset[str] | None` (None = unknown: keep today's behaviour). Nothing else changes.

New module: `installed_models(home: Path, host: str) -> frozenset[str] | None`. Lazily imports `spectracut.setup.plan.load_state`/`MODEL_PREFIX` and `spectracut.setup.model_assets.model_version`. Returns the ids whose state component `model:<id>` equals `model_version(id)` for `hosts[host]`, an empty set when the host is recorded but has no models (`--skip-models`), and None when the state file is missing or unreadable or has no record of the host.

(a) New `concept_skip_reason(config=None, *, runtime=None) -> str | None`: a reason naming the model id and host, e.g. "concept images skipped: image model 'z-image-turbo-q4' is not installed on model host 'legion'", when the local image model (`resolve_model("image", ...)`) is not in `getattr(runtime, 'installed', None)`. It returns None in mock mode, when runtime is None, when installed is None, or when `image_provider` is chatgpt. (b) `default_explorer` keeps its signature and returns None with a `logging` warning when there is a reason. (c) `PreproductionRunner.__init__` gains keywords `concept_note: str | None = None` and `note: Callable[[str, str], None] | None = None`. With no explorer and a concept_note, each style_frames/animatic build calls `note(ctx.spec.id, concept_note)` once. An explorer `ProviderError`/`OSError` in `_style_frames` or `_boards` logs a warning and leaves the remaining frames or boards of that build without a concept. It notes the node once with the error and does not count toward `image_exploration_requests`. The renderer and board_renderer still run, so the node succeeds.

`model_runtime()` passes `installed=installed_models(home, slot.name)` to both ModelRuntime constructions. `pre()` keeps calling `art_depts.default_explorer(runtime=runtime)` and also passes `concept_note=art_depts.concept_skip_reason(runtime=runtime)` and `note=<closure>` to PreproductionRunner. The closure calls `graph.add_note(node_id, RevisionNote(node_id=node_id, text=text, author="studio", created_at=<aware now>))` unless the same text is already among `graph.notes(node_id)`.

With the image model installed (or installed unknown, i.e. no setup-state record), default_explorer still returns the local RuntimeProvider (or ChatGPT when configured) and concept images plus `image_exploration_requests` usage are produced as before (src/spectracut/studio/departments/art.py:465-490, 541-543).

Mock mode (`SPECTRACUT_PROVIDERS=mock`) still returns the mock image provider from default_explorer; the M2 acceptance run (tests/acceptance/test_m2_preproduction.py via tests/acceptance/recorded/__init__.py) is unchanged.

ModelRuntime positional/keyword API (loader, pool, host=, clock=) and session/lease semantics in src/spectracut/providers/local/runtime.py are unchanged; existing constructions in tests and cli keep working.

Non-explorer failures in PreproductionRunner (renderer errors, missing board file, preview-tier refusal, voiced beat with no VO) still fail the node (src/spectracut/studio/departments/art.py:453-456, 527-528, 549-550).

decisions.choice: Use setup state (`<home>/setup-state.json`, component `model:<id>` == model_version(id)) as the installed-model query rather than a models-serve probe.
decisions.justification: It is local and free (no ssh round trip per run), and it is the same check setup itself uses to decide what is missing (src/spectracut/setup/plan.py:1052, model_assets.py:241). A host missing from state gives None (unknown), which keeps today's behaviour; the render-time degradation in D3 covers stale state and hand-installed hosts.

decisions.choice: Carry the installed set on ModelRuntime (`installed`) instead of adding a parameter to default_explorer.
decisions.justification: tests/cli/test_studio_run.py:778-784 fakes default_explorer with signature (config=None, *, runtime=None); studio.py:382 must keep that call shape. The runtime is already the shared per-run handle for sound and preproduction (src/spectracut/cli/studio.py:85-94).

decisions.choice: Record the skip as a graph node note (ProductionGraph.add_note, RevisionNote author="studio") through a callback, not RunResult.facts or a new StyleFrames field.
decisions.justification: studio run never constructs a FactsStore, so facts would be dropped (src/spectracut/studio/graph.py:861-862). Graph notes persist in the snapshot (graph.py:239) and are visible per node (graph.py:420-434). A new StyleFrames field would enter the LLM output schema of the style-frame artist (StyleFrames is validated as the department output at art.py:485).

src/spectracut/setup/plan.py:90 imports spectracut.studio.store, and providers.local is imported by studio.departments.art (art.py:46-48). A module-level import risks a cycle and loads setup's heavy imports for every provider user.

decisions.choice: Catch only ProviderError and OSError from the explorer; after the first failure, stop exploring for the rest of that build.
decisions.justification: The live failure is ProviderError (src/spectracut/providers/local/remote.py:111-114). Retrying a dead models-serve once per frame would spawn ssh repeatedly. ExecutorBusy (queue/executors/base.py:75) and programming errors still propagate.
